newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods gain with NYMEX, Gulf gasoline firms.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods gain with NYMEX, Gulf gasoline firms.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product prices moved higher late Thursday as NYMEX futures rebounded from the previous day's selloff and on firmer Gulf Coast gasoline differentials, traders said.
Spot futures prices surged higher early in the day, saw a brief setback near midday before settling near the intraday highs.

Gulf gasoline differentials ended the day slightly firmer, after whipsawing in wide range in active trade on the final day of scheduling for the 33rd cycle of the Colonial Pipeline, according to market players.
Prompt unleaded conventional M4 gasoline ended the day at 2.50 cents under the NYMEX, traders said, backing off from 1.25 cents under the print that was talked earlier in the day.

Some traders attrbiuted the flurry of trading in the M4 market to rumors that Exxon was having problems restarting a catalytic cracker at its Baytown, Texas refinery. But Exxon said all was well at the refinery following the restart of a reformer on Wednesday.
In New York Harbor, prompt No. 2 heating oil differentials softened slightly, though a lack of confirmed deals left the market at fairly notional levels.
